title: Polynomial substitution before desingularization quotients
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, A a finitely presented R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], Lambda an R-algebra, pi in R and alpha:A→Lambda. Assume pi is strictly standard [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] in A and a compatible section A/pi^4 A→R/pi^4 R exists. Then there are n,m,c, a presentation P of A with c≤m, coefficients s_ik,r_ji, elements lambda_i of Lambda, and polynomials g_j,e_j in Q=R[v_1,...,v_c,w_1,...,w_n] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put xi_i=pi^2 sum_k s_ik v_k+pi^3 w_i and F_j=P.relation_j(xi). They satisfy: g_j=v_j+sum_i r_ji w_i+pi e_j; F_j=pi^3 g_j for j<c; F_j∈(pi^2) for every j; pi F_j∈(g)+(F)^2 for every j; alpha(P.val_i)=pi^4 lambda_i. No annihilator stability or smoothness conclusion is assumed.

source.place: Stacks Project, Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CR (lemma-desingularize)

proof.text: Apply the translated-presentation theorem to obtain P, c<=min(n,m), lambda_i, relation constant coefficients pi^4 a_j, a scalar t, the constant minor membership for (1-pi^3 t)pi, and the original chosen-lift ideal-square conditions.

Form M_ij=constantCoeff(partial_i f_j) for j<c. Apply the first clause of scalar_left_inverse_maximal_minors to obtain S M=(1-pi^3 t)pi times the identity; set s_ik=S_ki. Reading the (k,j) entries and commuting scalars gives sum_i r_ji s_ik=(1-pi^3 t)pi delta_jk.

Prove first-order expansion by polynomial induction: f=C(constantCoeff f)+sum_i C(constantCoeff(partial_i f))X_i+q with q in the square of the variable ideal. Constants have zero remainder; remainders add under sums. For f X_i the first-order term is C(constantCoeff f)X_i, since constantCoeff(partial_j(f X_i)) is delta_ji constantCoeff f. The remainder is (the linear part of f+q)X_i, a product of two elements of the variable ideal. This is the proved private helper first_order_expansion, with no new hole.

Work directly with ULift-indexed variables V_j,W_i, and substitute xi_i=pi^2 sum_k s_ik V_k+pi^3 W_i. Every xi_i lies in (pi^2). Mapping the variable ideal gives an ideal contained in (pi^2), so mapping its square puts the remainder in (pi^4). Hence F_j=pi^4 b_j+sum_i r_ji xi_i for some polynomial b_j, and every F_j belongs to (pi^2). No element is cancelled.

For j<c, exchange the two finite sums in the linear term and use the scalar inverse to obtain sum_i r_ji xi_i=pi^3(V_j+sum_i r_ji W_i)-pi^6 t V_j. Explicitly set e_j=b_j-pi^2 t V_j and g_j=V_j+sum_i r_ji W_i+pi e_j. Ring arithmetic proves F_j=pi^3 g_j and the asserted formula for g_j.

Let I be the relation ideal and I0 the initial relation ideal. C(pi)-P.sigma(pi) belongs to I because evaluation kills this difference, and the presentation identifies its kernel with I. Multiplication by any relation puts the correction in I^2; adding it to the given condition yields C(pi)f_j in I0+I^2 for j>=c. For j<c the containment is immediate from membership in I0. The substitution maps I onto (F), and maps I0 into (g) since F_j=pi^3 g_j for initial j. Ideal maps commute with sums and squares, yielding C(pi)F_j in (g)+(F)^2 for every j. Return the lambda_i supplied by the translated presentation.
